A.explanation: Too small by about 10 orders of magnitude, implying atoms about $10^{-7} \text{ m}$ across, which is molecular or grain size not atomic size.

B.explanation: Matches $N \approx V/v_{atom}$ with $V = 5 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m}^3$ and $v_{atom} \approx 10^{-29} \text{ m}^3$, giving $N \approx 10^{24}$ to $10^{25}$.

C.explanation: Too large by about $10^4$, implying an atomic diameter much smaller than $10^{-10} \text{ m}$ and close to nuclear dimensions.

D.explanation: Too large by about $10^6$, implying far more atoms than can fit in $50 \text{ cm}^3$ with realistic atomic spacing.

hints: Start from the given $50 \text{ cm}^3$ and convert it to $\text{m}^3$ because atomic sizes are estimated in metres, with $1 \text{ cm}^3 = 10^{-6} \text{ m}^3$.
Recall a typical metal atom diameter of order $10^{-10} \text{ m}$, so one atom occupies a cube of volume of order $(10^{-10} \text{ m})^3 = 10^{-30} \text{ m}^3$ to $10^{-29} \text{ m}^3$.
Divide the total metal volume by the volume of one atom and compare the power of 10 with $10^{15}$, $10^{25}$, $10^{29}$ and $10^{31}$ to find the closest order of magnitude.
walkthrough: Convert the volume to SI units: $V = 50 \text{ cm}^3 = 50 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^3 = 5 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m}^3$.
Estimate the size of one metal atom: atomic diameter $d \approx 2 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$ to $3 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$, so treat one atom as a cube of side $\approx 10^{-10} \text{ m}$.
Estimate volume per atom: $v \approx d^3 \approx (10^{-10} \text{ m})^3 = 10^{-30} \text{ m}^3$, more realistically $10^{-29} \text{ m}^3$ allowing for packing.
Estimate number of atoms: $N \approx V/v \approx (5 \times 10^{-5})/(10^{-29}) = 5 \times 10^{24}$, which is order $10^{24}$ to $10^{25}$.
Check alternatives: $5 \times 10^{15}$ would need micron-sized atoms, while $10^{29}$ and $10^{31}$ would need atoms far smaller than $10^{-10} \text{ m}$.
The option closest to $10^{24}$ to $10^{25}$ is $5 \times 10^{25}$. This is option B.
